Table 3 reports nutrient CONCENTRATIONS - this is the primary target table for meta-analysis
Two species are reported separately (Q. myrtifolia and Q. geminata) plus combined totals - extract both species and the combined weighted mean
Weighted mean concentrations are provided for each species and combined 'Total vegetation' row in Table 3 - use these for meta-analysis
Litter (litterfall and standing litter) concentrations are also in Table 3 - these are NOT live plant tissue
Foliage and stem concentrations are reported separately within Table 3 - both are valid extraction targets
Some concentration differences are NOT statistically significant even though they appear in Table 3 - significance is marked with asterisks

The elevated CO2 level is described as 'ambient plus 350 µL/L', making absolute ppm unclear without knowing ambient; ambient at this site circa 1996-2001 was approximately 360-370 ppm, so elevated ≈ 710-720 ppm
n=8 chambers per treatment for vegetation/O horizon data, but soil data uses repeated measures across 1996 and 2001
Some soil data only available for 2001 (no 1996 baseline for C, N, S in soils)
BC horizon (21-60 cm) was not sampled in 1996, limiting pre-post comparisons
Laboratory bias noted for 1996 vs 2001 exchangeable cation analyses - authors excluded 1996 soil cation data
PRS probe data (Table 5) reports availability per 10 cm2 membrane area, not standard soil concentration units - use with caution
Unchambered control plots exist but are not the primary comparison; the primary comparison is ambient OTC vs elevated OTC

recon.treatment_definition: Elevated CO2 open-top chambers (8 chambers), ambient plus 350 µL/L CO2 (~710-720 ppm)
recon.potential_tc_confusion: None - labeling is clear and consistent throughout. However, note that unchambered control plots also exist but are not used in the primary CO2 comparison.
recon.sample_size_source: Of the 16 OTCs, 8 were maintained at current ambient CO2 and 8 at ambient plus 350 µL/L CO2 (elevated)
recon.extraction_guidance: CRITICAL: Table 3 is the only table with nutrient concentration data for meta-analysis. Table 2 has nutrient CONTENTS (kg/ha) which are ecosystem-level values, not concentrations. For meta-analysis of dilution effects, extract from Table 3 only. The 'Total vegetation' row at the bottom of the vegetation section gives the combined biomass-weighted mean across both species - this is the most appropriate single value for meta-analysis. Species-specific data (Q. myrtifolia and Q. geminata) can also be extracted as separate observations. Variance: Table 3 does NOT provide SE values - only significance asterisks (*P<0.05, **P<0.01, ***P<0.001). SE values for nutrient contents are in Table 2 but for contents not concentrations. This means variance data for concentrations in Table 3 cannot be directly extracted - this is a significant limitation. The elevated CO2 level is ambient + 350 µL/L; given circa 2000 ambient of ~370 ppm, elevated ≈ 720 ppm. n=8 per treatment (chambers). Do NOT extract from Table 5 (PRS probe data in µg/10cm2 - soil availability, not plant concentrations). Do NOT extract litter data if meta-analysis focuses on live plant tissue. The 'Weighted mean' rows in Table 3 represent foliage+stem combined for each species; 'Total vegetation' combines both species.
